# DatePicker & TimePicker

Figma: [03k. DatePicker & TimePicker](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-906) · Family: 03 Form & Input · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-26

Four components for selecting dates across Safqah - a Date Input trigger field that opens a platform-specific picker, a Wheel Picker for mobile (iOS-style scrolling wheels), a Calendar Picker for web (Material 3 month grid), and a Date Range Field that pairs two Date Inputs for start–end selection. Both Wheel and Calendar support single dates, ranges, and (calendar only) multi-select. The Wheel Picker also handles time and datetime modes.

### Date Input

A field with a calendar icon that shows a date and opens Date Wheel Picker on mobile or Date Calendar Picker on web.

Level: atom · Part of: Date Range Field

Use when:
- Date of birth or ID expiry in KYC
- A single date filter in transaction history
- Each side of a From / To range inside Date Range Field

Don't use when:
- Start and end dates together: use Date Range Field
- Free text dates typed by hand: do not use Input

Accessibility: Announce it as a button that opens a picker and read the chosen date in full (15 سبتمبر 2024).

### Date Wheel Picker

The mobile wheel picker opened as a sheet from Date Input, for dates, times or both, committed with an Apply button.

Level: organism

Use when:
- Picking a date of birth on mobile: Mode=single-date
- Time of day such as a reminder time: Mode=time
- Exact timestamps: Mode=datetime

Don't use when:
- Web and desktop date picking: use Date Calendar Picker
- Choosing an investment term from a few durations: use SegmentedControl_3 or Radio Group

Accessibility: Keep the 40dp selection row and hide or disable dates outside min and max instead of rejecting after selection.

### Date Calendar Picker

The web month-grid calendar popover opened from Date Input, for single, range or multi-date selection.

Level: organism

Use when:
- Date filters on back-office or web dashboards: Mode=single or range
- Picking non-contiguous days (rare): Mode=multi

Don't use when:
- Mobile date entry: use Date Wheel Picker
- Time selection: use Date Wheel Picker with Mode=time
- A From / To filter: use Date Range Field, not a two-month calendar

Accessibility: Support arrow-key navigation and Enter, and keep 40dp day cells.

### Date Range Field

Two Date Inputs side by side (من / إلى) for a start and end date, each opening its own picker. This is the Safqah range pattern on mobile and web.

Level: organism · Contains: Date Input

Use when:
- Transaction history or statement period filters
- Deal duration or payout window filters

Don't use when:
- A single date: use Date Input
- Preset periods such as 30 days or 3 months: use SegmentedControl_3 or Tag Group

Accessibility: Label each input distinctly (من, إلى) and validate that the end is not before the start.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Date Picker is the date entry system for Safqah. The same Date Input trigger field is used across mobile and web - the difference is what opens when the user taps it: a wheel picker on mobile (iOS convention), a calendar popover on web (desktop convention). For ranges, the Date Range Field pairs two Date Inputs that each open their own picker, matching the "من/إلى" pattern from the existing Safqah product.

Common Safqah use cases: birth date entry (KYC), deal duration filters ("last 30 days", "Q4 2024"), commitment period selection, payout schedule, transaction history filters, agreement validity period. The mode (single / range / multi) and the precision (date / time / datetime) are configured per-instance - pick the right picker for the workflow.

### At a glance

### Atomic architecture

Four components: one trigger atom + two picker organisms (mobile vs web) + one range composition. The Date Input is shared across all flows - what changes is the picker that opens.

Atom - Date Input · 36 variants

Trigger field with calendar icon + placeholder/value. Variants: 3 sizes × 6 states × 2 directions. Identical to other form inputs visually (matches the Input organism height and chrome) - the only difference is the icon and the picker that opens on tap. Use anywhere a date is being selected.

Mobile organism - Date Wheel Picker · 8 variants

iOS-style scrolling wheel picker. Opens as a bottom sheet from a Date Input tap on mobile. Variants: 4 modes (single-date / date-range / time / datetime) × 2 directions. The Apply button commits the selection. Native iOS/Android pattern users immediately recognize.

Web organism - Date Calendar Picker · 6 variants

Material 3 month-grid calendar. Opens as a popover from a Date Input click on web. Variants: 3 modes (single / range / multi) × 2 directions. Today shown with outline, selected day(s) filled green, range shows start+end with implicit fill between. Prev/next month arrows in the header.

Composition - Date Range Field · 30 variants

Pair of Date Inputs (From + To) for selecting a start–end range. Variants: 3 sizes × 5 states × 2 directions. RTL flips the visual order (To on the left, From on the right) and uses Arabic labels (من/إلى). Each input opens its own picker - wheel on mobile, calendar on web. Matches the existing Safqah "من/إلى" pattern from the reference design.

### Mobile vs web - pick the right picker

The same Date Input field opens different pickers on mobile and web. This is the single most important decision when designing date entry - match the platform convention or users will fight the UI.

Mobile · Wheel Picker

Tap a Date Input field → wheel picker slides up from the bottom of the screen as a sheet. User scrolls month / day / year wheels independently, taps Apply to commit. Matches iOS UIDatePicker and Android Material BottomSheet patterns. Best for touch input where typing dates would be slow and error-prone.

Web · Calendar Picker

Click a Date Input field → calendar popover anchors to the field. Month grid lets user scan visually, navigate months with prev/next arrows, click any day to select. Optional keyboard support (arrow keys, Enter to confirm). Matches Material 3 / Adobe Spectrum / Stripe conventions. Best for desktop where mouse scanning and keyboard navigation are faster than wheel scrolling.

> **Tip:** Platform detection: use the runtime's platform check (Flutter's Theme.of(context).platform, Material vs Cupertino) to render the correct picker. Don't expose the choice as a prop - picker convention is a platform contract, not a feature toggle. If you NEED the same picker across platforms (rare), document why.

### Modes

The Wheel Picker supports four modes for precise control over what gets picked. The Calendar Picker supports three (no time selection in calendar form).

### Wheel modes (mobile)

single-date

3 wheels: Month / Day / Year. Use for birth date, deal launch date, single-day deadlines.

date-range

Single date wheel used twice - once for From and once for To. Each opens independently from its Date Input.

time

2 wheels: Hour / Minute. Use for time-of-day selection (meeting time, payout cutoff).

datetime

4 wheels: Month / Day / Hour / Minute. Use for precise event timestamps (transaction recording, scheduled publishing).

### Calendar modes (web)

single

One date selected. Today shown with outline, selected day filled green. Click any day to reassign selection. The most common mode.

range

Start + end dates with implicit highlight between them. First click sets start, second click sets end. Click outside the range to reset. Used for date filters, deal duration, transaction history windows.

multi

Multiple independent dates selected. Click toggles each date on/off. Use sparingly - only for cases where users need to pick non-contiguous days (e.g., available office days, exception dates).

### States - Date Input

The Date Input field follows the form-family state pattern. Six states cover the full input lifecycle.

default

Resting empty state. Placeholder "From" / "من", neutral border.

filled

Date selected. Value displayed in default text color ("15 سبتمبر 2024"), neutral border.

hover

Mouse hover (desktop only). Subtle border darkening to signal interactivity.

focus

Field active (clicked / tab-focused). Dark border + focus ring. Picker dialog usually opens automatically on focus.

error

Invalid date entered (manual typing) or no date selected when required. Red border. Pair with a Form Field Helper to explain.

disabled

Field is inert. Reduced opacity. Use when date is system-determined (e.g., "Created on" is read-only).

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Both pickers and the Date Range Field flip layout for Arabic. The wheel picker reorders its wheels (year / day / month from left to right in RTL, with Arabic month names). The calendar picker keeps its grid structure but reverses column order and uses Arabic day labels. The Range Field flips the From/To visual order.

LTR

English / default. Wheel columns: Month / Day / Year. Calendar columns: S/M/T/W/T/F/S. Date Range Field: From on the left, To on the right. Apply button label: "Apply".

RTL

Arabic. Wheel columns reorder: Year / Day / Month (right-to-left reading). Arabic month names: يناير / فبراير / ... / ديسمبر. Calendar columns reverse: س / ج / خ / ر / ث / ن / ح. Range Field: To on the left, From on the right. Apply button label: "تطبيق".

> **Tip:** Arabic month names: use the long form (يناير، فبراير، مارس، إبريل، مايو، يونيو، يوليو، أغسطس، سبتمبر، أكتوبر، نوفمبر، ديسمبر). Don't abbreviate to 3 letters like English Jan/Feb - Arabic readers expect full names in formal financial contexts like Safqah. The wheel auto-trims visual overflow.

### Range pattern - the من/إلى Safqah convention

For date ranges on Safqah, use the Date Range Field - a pair of Date Inputs side by side, where each input opens its own picker. This is the established pattern from the existing Safqah product (the reference design at design file 0EsfJp3Tzwn4DgfoI7Z64l, node 9829:114683) and matches user expectations from competing products (Tameed, Forus, Raqamyah, banking apps).

Why two inputs, not a single trigger that opens a two-month calendar? Three reasons: (1) Mobile users on Safqah do most of their date entry through wheels, not calendars, so a two-month calendar wouldn't work on mobile. (2) The two-input pattern is platform-agnostic - same UI on mobile and web. (3) Users can independently re-pick the From or To without re-confirming the other.

LTR and RTL Date Range Field

> **Warning:** Don't build a custom "two-month calendar in a popover" pattern. Even though it's a common web convention (Airbnb, Booking.com), it doesn't match the existing Safqah experience and creates inconsistency between mobile (wheel) and web (calendar). Stick with the Date Range Field for all platforms.

### Code examples

How to consume DatePicker components in Flutter.

### Flutter - basic single date selection

```dart
// Single date selection - mobile (wheel) and web (calendar)
class _BirthDateFieldState extends State<BirthDateField> {
  DateTime? _selectedDate;
  
  Future<void> _pickDate() async {
    final picked = await showSafqahDatePicker(
      context: context,
      initialDate: _selectedDate ?? DateTime.now(),
      firstDate: DateTime(1950),
      lastDate: DateTime.now(),
      mode: DatePickerMode.singleDate,
    );
    if (picked != null) {
      setState(() => _selectedDate = picked);
    }
  }
  
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return SafqahDateInput(
      label: 'Date of birth',
      value: _selectedDate,
      placeholder: 'Select your birth date',
      onTap: _pickDate,
      isRequired: true,
    );
  }
}
```

### Flutter - date range with two inputs

```dart
// Date range using two SafqahDateInputs (the من/إلى Safqah pattern)
class _DealDurationFilterState extends State<DealDurationFilter> {
  DateTime? _from;
  DateTime? _to;
  
  Future<void> _pickFrom() async {
    final picked = await showSafqahDatePicker(
      context: context,
      initialDate: _from ?? DateTime.now(),
      lastDate: _to ?? DateTime.now().add(const Duration(days: 365)),
    );
    if (picked != null) setState(() => _from = picked);
  }
  
  Future<void> _pickTo() async {
    final picked = await showSafqahDatePicker(
      context: context,
      initialDate: _to ?? _from?.add(const Duration(days: 30)) ?? DateTime.now(),
      firstDate: _from ?? DateTime(2020),
    );
    if (picked != null) setState(() => _to = picked);
  }
  
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Row(
      children: [
        Expanded(
          child: SafqahDateInput(
            label: 'From',
            value: _from,
            placeholder: 'From',
            onTap: _pickFrom,
          ),
        ),
        const SizedBox(width: 12),
        Expanded(
          child: SafqahDateInput(
            label: 'To',
            value: _to,
            placeholder: 'To',
            onTap: _pickTo,
          ),
        ),
      ],
    );
  }
}
```

### Flutter - Arabic RTL context

```dart
// Arabic locale - wheel uses Arabic month names automatically
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: SafqahDateInput(
    label: 'تاريخ الميلاد',  // "Date of birth"
    value: _selectedDate,
    placeholder: 'اختر تاريخ ميلادك',
    onTap: () async {
      final picked = await showSafqahDatePicker(
        context: context,
        initialDate: _selectedDate ?? DateTime.now(),
        firstDate: DateTime(1950),
        lastDate: DateTime.now(),
        locale: const Locale('ar', 'SA'),  // triggers Arabic month names + "تطبيق"
      );
      if (picked != null) setState(() => _selectedDate = picked);
    },
  ),
)
```

### Flutter - datetime picker for transaction timestamps

```dart
// Datetime mode - pick exact moment for transaction recording
SafqahDateInput(
  label: 'Transaction time',
  value: _txTime,
  placeholder: 'Select date and time',
  onTap: () async {
    final picked = await showSafqahDatePicker(
      context: context,
      initialDate: _txTime ?? DateTime.now(),
      firstDate: DateTime.now().subtract(const Duration(days: 30)),
      lastDate: DateTime.now(),
      mode: DatePickerMode.dateTime,  // 4-wheel: month / day / hour / minute
    );
    if (picked != null) setState(() => _txTime = picked);
  },
  helperText: 'Used to backdate manual transactions only',
  helperTone: HelperTone.info,
)
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts.

- **Do** · Date entry on mobile: Use the Date Input + Wheel Picker combination on mobile. Tapping the Date Input opens the wheel as a bottom sheet. Native pattern, no typing required, low error rate. Even on touch keyboards, wheel scrolling is faster than typing dates.
- **Don't** · Date entry on mobile: Don't use HTML <input type="date"> on mobile without testing across iOS Safari and Android Chrome - browser implementations vary wildly. Don't use the calendar picker on mobile - the tap targets become unreadably small on phones below 6 inches.
- **Do** · Date range filter on desktop dashboard: Use the Date Range Field - two Date Inputs side by side. Each click opens its own calendar popover. User picks From first, then To. Works the same as the existing Safqah deal duration filter. Matches Tameed / Forus conventions users already know.
- **Don't** · Date range filter on desktop dashboard: Don't build a custom "two-month calendar in a popover" (Airbnb/Booking style). Don't use a single input with " - " separator for the range - manual typing is error-prone (formats vary: 2024-09-17 vs 17/09/2024 vs 17 Sep 2024). Don't require typing at all for date ranges.
- **Do** · Arabic RTL date entry: Use the RTL Direction variant. Date Input shows the calendar icon on the left (leading edge in Arabic), placeholder/value right-aligned. Wheel picker uses Arabic month names ("سبتمبر" not "September") and "تطبيق" (Apply) button label. Calendar uses Arabic day headers (س/ج/خ/ر/ث/ن/ح).
- **Don't** · Arabic RTL date entry: Don't use LTR direction in Arabic contexts. Don't mix English month names with RTL layout ("Sep" in an RTL field). Don't use the Latin Apply button label in Arabic UIs - use "تطبيق". Don't abbreviate Arabic month names to 3 letters; use full names ("سبتمبر" not "سبت").
- **Do** · Required vs optional date fields: Use the error state when a required date is missing after a submit attempt. Pair with a Form Field Helper showing the specific issue ("Date of birth is required" or "Please select a valid date"). Red border focuses user attention on the problem field.
- **Don't** · Required vs optional date fields: Don't leave required dates in the default state after a failed submit. Don't show a generic "Please complete all fields" message at the top - inline errors anchored to the specific field are more actionable. Don't use the error state preemptively (before the user has had a chance to fill the field).

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Info:** Wheel as mobile pattern, calendar as web pattern - this isn't a feature toggle, it's a platform contract. The runtime framework code uses Theme.of(context).platform (or equivalent) to pick the right picker. Designers don't need to design both pickers for every flow; one Date Input handles both.

> **Info:** The Date Range Field is the established Safqah pattern (referenced from file 0EsfJp3Tzwn4DgfoI7Z64l, node 9829:114683). Two inputs side by side, each opening its own picker. Works identically on mobile and web. Matches user expectations from Tameed, Forus, Raqamyah, and other Saudi fintech competitors.

> **Info:** Why no "Range Calendar" component (two months side by side in one popover)? Three reasons: (1) It doesn't work on mobile, so you'd need both patterns and inconsistent UX between platforms. (2) The two-input pattern matches the existing Safqah product, so we avoid retraining users. (3) The Date Range Field gives users independent control over From and To - they can edit one without touching the other. The two-month calendar forces them to "reset" by clicking outside the range.

> **Warning:** RTL implementation hits the locked constraint #11 problem (TEXT property defaultValue takes from first variant). Workaround: removed componentPropertyReferences.characters on RTL variants and set Arabic text directly. This means runtime overrides of Value text work on LTR variants but RTL variants have hardcoded Arabic until overridden per-instance. Flagged for follow-up if a cleaner pattern emerges.

> **Warning:** The Date Range Field "To" input also needs to display "To" / "إلى" not "From" / "من" - required removing the property reference on the To input's value-text node and setting the text directly per variant. Without this, both inputs showed "From".

> **Info:** Calendar mode "multi" is a less common pattern - used for picking non-contiguous days. Most date entry on Safqah is single or range. Keep multi for edge cases (availability calendars, exception dates). Don't default to multi without a strong reason.

> **Info:** The wheel picker's scrolling behavior is critical - items above and below the center selection fade out gradually (text/muted). Selected center item is bold + text/default. This visual emphasis tells users where the "select" line is. Don't flatten the wheel into a list with all items at equal weight.

> **Tip:** Arabic month names use the long form (يناير، فبراير، مارس، إبريل، مايو، يونيو، يوليو، أغسطس، سبتمبر، أكتوبر، نوفمبر، ديسمبر). Don't abbreviate to 3 letters even in compact contexts. The wheel naturally truncates if a name is too long. For the Date Input field, full Arabic month names + year fit comfortably in lg/md sizes but may truncate in sm - test before shipping with sm + RTL.

> **Tip:** Min/max date constraints - set them at the picker level, not in field validation. The picker should show invalid dates as disabled (muted, not tappable) rather than letting users select then reject. For the wheel, this means hiding (or fading) wheel rows outside the range. For the calendar, day cells outside firstDate/lastDate are styled as disabled.

> **Info:** Time mode and datetime mode are wheel-only - the calendar picker doesn't support time selection. If a workflow needs date + time in one screen, use the datetime wheel mode on both mobile and web (override platform detection). The 4-wheel datetime gets cramped on narrow desktop popovers but works.

> **Warning:** WCAG WARNING - calendar day cells at the standard size (40dp) pass WCAG 2.5.5 AA on touch. The wheel picker selection row is 40dp tall by default, which also passes. Don't shrink either component below these defaults even for dense desktop layouts - accessibility matters more than visual density.

> **Warning:** FONT WORKAROUND - Same as the rest of the form family. All text uses IBM Plex Sans Regular/Medium/SemiBold. Font/Size, Font/Line-Height, and Font/Weight all bound to variables on every text node.
